newsitem.title: USA: Dollar takes breather, ends lackluster session mixed.
newsitem.headline: Dollar takes breather, ends lackluster session mixed.

text.p: The dollar ended mixed in a lackluster trading session Wednesday as currency dealers took a breather following two highly active and volatile sessions on Monday and Tuesday.
"The market is definitely a little shell-shocked," said Lisa Finstrom, foreign exchange analyst at Smith Barney Inc. "I'm not quite sure if people knew what hit them earlier in the week."

The dollar ended the session modestly higher against the mark at 1.5605, up from 1.5565 on Tuesday. Against the yen, the greenback traded in an extremely tight range throughout the day before closing at 113.07, down from 113.37.
Yen strength, albeit modest, was the predominant theme of the day, with the Japanese currency pushing higher against most European currencies, as well as the dollar.

Aiding the yen were remarks from former Japanese Ministry of Finance official Makoto Utsumi, who reinforced the market's conviction that Japanese authorities do not want the dollar to climb beyond its recent highs near 115 yen.
Utsumi said Wednesday that a 105 to 115 yen range versus the dollar was appropriate and an accurate reflection of economic fundamentals in the two countries.

"I think you'll see the yen continue to strengthen relative to other currencies," said John McCarthy, foreign exchange manager at ING Barings Capital Markets. "If you think the dollar has room to move up, it's going to move up against Europe a lot easier than it is against the yen."

Keeping the dollar in check Wednesday were weak U.S. markets. The Dow Jones industrial average fell over 70 points in the afternoon, before trimming its losses to end the session only 19.75 points lower at 6422.94.
Bonds stumbled lower as well, disappointed when the Federal Reserve failed to add permanent reserves to the banking system, as many in the market had expected.

"The bond market came off quite heavily and the Dow Jones industrials were down as well," said Hans Boman, chief spot dealer at Swedbank. "I think some dollar weakness is related to the bonds and stocks."
The British pound, which tumbled Tuesday after reports that British exporters were concerned about its recent strength, rose modestly against the dollar Wednesday, ending at $1.6433, against $1.6425.
Elsewhere, the dollar was relatively flat at 1.3205 Swiss francs, compared with 1.3207 on Tuesday, and modestly higher at Canadian $1.3538 versus C$1.3503.
